M-S-002.mitigation: Use PKI systems and digital certificates

M-S-003.mitigation: Implement secure session management with proper timeout

M-S-004.mitigation: Use digitally signed packets and authenticate code/data

M-S-006.mitigation: Use centralized account management with revocation capability (LDAP, Active Directory, RADIUS, IAM)

M-S-007.mitigation: Enforce default-deny policy at trust boundary — only explicitly permitted traffic is allowed (NDR 5.2 RE1)

M-S-008.mitigation: Implement hardware authentication (secure elements, cryptographic chips)

M-S-009.mitigation: Authenticate each sensor per device (device keys/certificates, signed readings) with freshness/anti-replay (nonce, timestamp or counter); where per-device crypto is infeasible on legacy/analog field devices, compensate with zone/conduit segmentation (IEC 62443-3-3 SR 5.1) and continuous plausibility monitoring

M-S-010.mitigation: Bind the sensor to a provisioned identity at commissioning; reject unprovisioned sources

M-S-011.mitigation: Plausibility and rate checks to detect injected, out-of-profile readings

M-S-012.mitigation: Authenticate the command source over an authenticated control channel; where per-device crypto is infeasible on legacy/analog field devices, compensate with zone/conduit segmentation (IEC 62443-3-3 SR 5.1)

M-S-013.mitigation: Enforce a command authorization policy (only permitted controllers)

M-S-015.mitigation: Verify actuation through an independent measurement / closed-loop feedback rather than trusting the actuator's own status report
